title: The same notes, a different home
summary: Compare C major with A minor.

steps.title: The same notes, a different home
steps.body:
**relative minor** means the minor key that shares a major key’s notes. A minor is the relative minor of C major. **relative major** names the other direction: C major is the relative major of A minor. Their notes match, but their tonic differs.

**Why it matters:** Sharing notes does not make two keys identical; listen for the note that feels like home.

steps.title: Find the notes
steps.body: C major uses C, D, E, F, G, A, B. A natural minor uses A, B, C, D, E, F, G. Play the same letters but begin and finish on a different home.

items.prompt: Play A, B, C, D, E, F, G, A in that order, one note at a time.

steps.title: Make it familiar
steps.body: Play C major, finishing on C. Then play A natural minor, finishing on A. Let the final note ring before comparing.
